profiles.summary: No opcode, jump or memory result differs from the specification at head 52,411,109. The battery, the targeted set, both PoolManager script sets, the mined swap check and the replay give the cycle 34 counts on the official node. The replicas still run nanoreth f0cad31 and b92ad36 on revm 43 with ruint 1.20.1, and no crate, tag or advisory is newer. One fact is new: the nanoreth release notes call reth v2.8.1 the last revm-based reth release, so the next nanoreth that follows upstream reth will run the evm2 interpreter. The validator binary is still not served.

deltas.delta: The nb-20261125-2 release notes (b92ad36) state that reth v2.8.1 (revm 43) is the last revm-based reth release. A later nanoreth on newer reth would move the public replicas to evm2. Cycle 34 read evm2 at reth main e80df9c4 and found that only DIV and MOD change form, to checked division that still returns 0 for a zero divisor, with 198,071 division vectors matching. The change concerns replicas, which are the review's evidence clients. It does not concern the closed hl-node that produces blocks.

On testnet the EIP-2935 history contract holds code with nonce 1, but its ring buffer slots for the last blocks are zero and do not hold the block hashes. The contract was deployed by an ordinary transaction, and no Prague system call writes to it. Testnet therefore shows no partial activation of Prague.

profiles.summary: The PoolManager has emitted one log since block 52,371,153, the Swap of block 52,388,737 that cycle 34 already checked. In that block the official endpoint's receipts equal the archive replica's, and the block hash and receipts root are equal. No new block holds the failed-then-later pattern of L-1269 or the wide FullMath and fee-copy inputs of L-1271, so neither lead can be answered from mined data. The PoolManager still has no HyperCore account and its nonce is 1.

The precompile set 0x0800 to 0x0814 is unchanged, as is the empty range 0x0815 to 0x083f. CoreWriter, the HYPE system address, WHYPE, the USDC contract and 0xb883... carry the same code hashes as in cycle 34. Only the oracle and price words that the read precompiles return have moved. The published linking rule for an EVM contract deployed by another contract names the contract's first storage slot or the slot at keccak256("HyperCore deployer") as the finalizer. In the PoolManager the first storage slot holds the owner, so only governance could finalize a link naming the PoolManager.

deltas.delta: The HyperCore to HyperEVM transfer page states the finalizer rule for linking a Core token to an EVM contract: for a contract deployed by an EOA, the deploying EOA signs with the deploy nonce; for a contract deployed by a contract, the address stored in the first storage slot or in slot keccak256("HyperCore deployer") signs. For the PoolManager these are its deployer and its owner 0x2d09d0c2...21f9 (slot 0, Owned), so an ordinary account cannot link a Core token to the PoolManager address.

profiles.summary: No HyperEVM fork is announced. The API channel lists HyperCore network upgrades on 6, 12, 13 and 21 November 2026, the 200,000 gas cap on sendToEvmWithData, the 1 USDC minimum for HyperEVM to HyperCore transfers, L1 errors in HyperEVM error responses and the nb-20261125-2 replica release. All of these were recorded by earlier cycles. The main channel's newest posts (16 and 20 November) name no EVM change. HIP-3 permissioned markets are scheduled for a future HyperCore upgrade and do not touch the PoolManager, which has no HyperCore account. The validator remains a single closed binary, hl-node, which returns HTTP 403, and hl-visor is byte equal.

cleared.check: Can an ordinary account link a HyperCore spot token to the PoolManager address, so that HyperCore credits or debits through it?
cleared.result: No. Finalizing a link to a contract deployed by a contract needs a signature from the address held in the contract's first storage slot or in slot keccak256("HyperCore deployer"). The PoolManager's slot 0 holds its owner. No mapping slot of the PoolManager can equal a fixed hash without a preimage. The PoolManager also exposes no ERC-20 transfer(address,uint256) and no fallback, and its ERC-6909 Transfer event has a different topic from the ERC-20 Transfer that HyperCore reads.

leads.question: When a nanoreth release built on reth after v2.8.1 (evm2) appears, do the battery, the targeted set and the PoolManager scripts still match on a replica that runs it, and does that replica still reproduce the receipts root of the closed producer's blocks?
leads.why: The replicas are the only public check on HyperEVM's closed producer. A replica on a new interpreter that silently tolerated a mismatch would weaken every mined-data clearance for chain 999.

leadResults.answer: Operator level, recorded for reference. No public query or binary shows the rule. The info endpoint still returns HTTP 422 for alignedQuoteTokenInfo with and without a token. For the PoolManager, userRole is missing, spotClearinghouseState has no balances and userNonFundingLedgerUpdates is empty, so no HyperCore transfer has ever named it. hl-visor contains no string about aqa, treasury or aligned quote, and hl-node is not served (HTTP 403). The only published rule naming contract addresses is the link finalizer rule (first storage slot or slot keccak256("HyperCore deployer")). That rule does not cover the AQAv2 treasury designation.

No instance exists yet. Between block 52,371,153 and head 52,411,376 the PoolManager emitted one log, the Swap of block 52,388,737. That block holds a single PoolManager transaction, and its receipts, hash and receipts root equal the archive replica's. The cycle 34 result therefore stands: every failed PoolManager transaction above a completed unlock was the last PoolManager transaction of its block.

No mined block holds such a call. The PoolManager has had one transaction since block 52,371,153, a Swap in an existing pool. The 2 swaps of the newest window (52,104,259 to 52,411,238) satisfy the tick relation. The 85,544 targeted vectors, which include 21,074 vectors of the 512 bit mulDiv shape, again return the reference words through eth_call on the official node. Whether that path is the producer's path remains unknown, as cycle 24 recorded. This review sends no transaction.
